Saving some documents fails with a Postgres error. It happens when the text is
mostly unique tokens: hashes, IDs, base64, long tables of numbers. The document
search trigger caps its input at 1,000,000 characters, but Postgres's tsvector
size limit applies to the output, so a document under the cap can still produce
a search vector that's too big. The save errors out, the worker task that
refreshes the document text keeps retrying and failing, and the text and search
index go stale.

Saving such a document must succeed. When the full text produces a search
vector that is too large, index as much of the text as fits instead (at least
the beginning of the text). The title and the previous titles must still be
fully indexed, with their usual weights.

Work within this local repository and the context you have been given. Do not
look up this project or its history online.

Verify your work before you finish: add or update automated tests that cover
the change, run them together with the existing tests for the code you touched,
and make sure they pass.

Documents whose text produces too large a search vector now save normally. In that case only as much of the beginning of the text as fits gets indexed. The new tests and the existing related tests pass.

**The fix** is a new migration, `server/migrations/20261019120000-handle-oversized-document-search-vector.js`, that redefines `documents_search_trigger()`:
- The title (weight A) and previous titles (weight C) are always indexed in full, as before.
- It first tries the text up to the existing 1,000,000-character cap, exactly as today. When that fits, the search vector is the same as before.
- If Postgres rejects it with "string is too long for tsvector", the trigger catches that error and narrows down to a prefix of the text that fits. That prefix is indexed at weight D, so the save succeeds.
- The size error can also come from joining the title, previous titles and text together, not just from processing the text. I checked that this raises the same error code, so it's caught too.
- `down` restores the previous trigger function.

**Trade-offs:**
- The prefix search stops once it's within about 1% of the true limit, so it may index slightly less text than would fit.
- The cut can land mid-word, so the last indexed token may be a fragment.
- Saving an oversized document is slower, because Postgres processes the text several times while narrowing down. Normal documents take one try; the only extra cost is a lightweight error-handling block.

**Tests** are in `server/models/Document.test.ts`, under a new `searchVector` block. The test text is about 30,000 MD5 hashes, which stays under the 1M-character cap but makes Postgres fail:
- **Normal document:** the title is indexed at weight A and the text at weight D.
- **Oversized document on create:** the save succeeds, the title and the start of the text are indexed, and a word at the end isn't.
- **Oversized document on update:** this is the path the text-refresh worker uses. The save succeeds, the text is stored, the current title is indexed at A and the old title at C, and the stale text is gone from the index.

**Verification:**
- With the migration rolled back, both oversized-document tests fail with the "string is too long for tsvector" error; with it applied, they pass.
- `Document.test.ts` plus the search tests (`PostgresSearchProvider`, `SearchIndexProcessor`, `SearchQuery`, the searches API, `CleanupOldSearchQueriesTask`): 134 tests, all passing.
- `yarn tsc`, oxfmt and oxlint are clean.

The migration only changes how future saves are indexed. Documents that are already stale will be indexed when they're next saved, for example when the retrying worker task next runs.
